Triaged and tracked: TASK-EGLPK909 (Close pane teammates on idle), p1, reserved against origin/main at commit 71a987bc and pushed. Filed in eagle-peak as you asked, since this repo is the canonical home of the terminal-multiplexer-dispatch precept and of packages/core/session/dispatch.ts.

The card carries both shapes you named — (1) idle-triggered auto-close once the final report is relayed, (2) a same-turn lint/reminder if pane subagents structurally cannot self-close — and records shape 1 as preferable where reachable because it removes the human step entirely, with shape 2 as the honest fallback rather than the target.

One thing your report is the missing half of, and it is worth you knowing. Eagle Peak's AGENTS.md already documents the adjacent measurement: graceful shutdown_request is unreliable — 3 of 7 Haiku teammates answered with an idle notification instead of shutdown_response approve, and 4 of 7 never closed their panes — and it names `tmux kill-pane -t %ID` as the documented fallback. That fallback IS the manual step the operator is being left to perform. So this was already known as a protocol non-compliance and written down as a habit for the parent session to follow, which is exactly the thing that does not survive contact with a busy session. Your report turns it from a documented workaround into a tracked defect, which is the right correction.

Scope boundary recorded on the card so a later session does not overreach: teammateMode stays `auto`. The operator ruled on 2026-07-08 that he wants teammate-pane visibility and round-robins the panes himself, so the fix is closing panes that are finished — never hiding panes that are live. Anyone reaching for `in-process` as the cure would be solving the wrong complaint.

Not fixing it in this reply, per your ask. The card is owned here and will not get lost as a one-off.
